H.R. 2869 IGNORES EBSA'S FUNDING NEEDS
Insufficient funding has resulted in steady declines in full-time employees (full-time equivalents or FTEs) at EBSA. In FY2015, EBSA received $181 million in appropriations to support 963 FTEs.\27\ A decade later, EBSA received $191 million in its base appropriation in FY25, supporting only 687 FTEs.\28\ The Trump Administration's recent budget proposes to cut that number to just 640.\29\ If EBSA funding had been maintained in inflation-adjusted terms since FY15, EBSA would have received $243.7 million in appropriations in FY25. Republicans pursued a further cut in their continuing resolution introduced on September 16, 2025\30\ by excluding the Department from an extension of critical resources to enforce the bipartisan No Surprises Act--a cut that will effectively be a giveaway to insurance companies that will threaten patients who are supposed to be protected from surprise medical bills. This cut was ultimately enacted on November 12, 2025.\31\

This decline in EBSA capacity detracts from its ability to assist and educate workers, plan sponsors, fiduciaries, and service providers. It further hampers the agency's enforcement efforts. In 2024, the then-Assistant Secretary of EBSA appeared before the Committee's Subcommittee on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) and testified that EBSA has less than one investigator for every 13,900 ERISA-covered health, retirement, and other benefit plans.\32\ Despite drastic cuts to EBSA and its enforcement capacity, H.R. 2869 adds new and incomplete reporting requirements that will demand employee time and attention, may undermine the best interest of workers and their families, and does not give any credence to the effectiveness of EBSA's efforts.
\32\Examining the Policies and Priorities of the Employee Benefits Security Administration: Hearing Before the Subcomm. on Health, Emp't, Lab., and Pensions of the H. Comm. on Educ. & the Workforce, 118th Cong. 6 (2024) (statement of Lisa Gomez, Administrator, Employee Benefits Security Administration).
CONCLUSION
Committee Democrats support meaningful transparency and accountability from the Department, but H.R. 2869 would not provide that. The bill requires a one-sided report that fails to provide a fulsome picture of EBSA's work and appears designed to portray the agency in a negative light. The bill also adds to EBSA's administrative burden without authorizing any additional resources for them to do the work. For the reasons stated above, Committee Democrats unanimously opposed H.R. 2869 when the Committee on Education and Workforce considered it on September 17, 2025. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
Robert C. ``Bobby'' Scott,
Ranking Member.
Suzanne Bonamici,
Alma S. Adams,
Mark DeSaulnier,
Jahana Hayes,
Summer Lee,
Members of Congress.
